# The `view`/`ask` corpus: sources, builder and the first slice

Owner decisions: DECISIONS.md, "2026-10-09 — representation chosen by use" and "2026-10-09 — one summarizer family:
`view` and `ask`". The corpus is artifact-diverse (prose, code, HTML, JSON/YAML, tables, logs and tool outputs). Its
targets are static: reconstruction, code-computed extraction and identifier retention, plus questions and summaries
**taken from existing public datasets**. Nothing in it is generated by a teacher model (a quality rule). Data is
registered with manifests. Every dataset licence is acceptable (owner rule 2026-10-10, AGENTS.md): licences are recorded
per record as provenance facts, and no source is omitted or held for its licence. Training admission is gated only on
the view operator stage's qualification.

- Builder: `scripts/neuralese_data/view_corpus.py` (records), `view_extract.py` (extraction engines),
  `view_sources.py` (pinned downloads); entry point `scripts/neuralese_view_corpus.py {fetch,build}`.
- Tests: `tests/neuralese/test_view_corpus.py` (fixtures only, no downloads).
- Raw downloads: `/mnt/external/natlang-development-data/data/neuralese/raw/view-sources-20261009/` with
  `sources.json` (URL, revision, SHA-256, size and licence per file).
- First slice: see §5; current corpus `view-ask-20261010-v3` (§5.3).

## 1. Record shape

Records are `natlang.port-record/1` (S1_DATA.md §2.1). They are validated by `scripts/neuralese_data/records.py`
(contract, markup, leakage) and by the trainer's loader `training/neuralese/natlang_neuralese/data/records.py`. The
schema was not changed. The conventions specific to this corpus are:

| Field | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `family` | `view_<artifact>_<kind>`: artifact is prose, code, html, data (JSON/YAML), table or log; kind is reconstruct, summary, qa or extract |
| `task` | `reconstruct` for `view(x)` read back (target = source). `consume` for a single purpose over a source. `compare` when one source carries several purposes: all of that source's purposeful records become `compare` and list each other in `contrasts.purpose_pairs` |
| `sources` | one source, except **multi-source records** (v3, Multi-News): several documents (each a source with role `document`, titles `article 1`, `article 2`, …) and one purpose, `view(xs, instructions)` over the list. They are `consume` records (no reconstruction: one value per reconstruction). The view-stage conversion renders the list as one value, the documents in order each under a `Document k of n:` line (`view_records.value_text`; the gate uses the same rendering) |
| `writer.instructions` | the purpose: the dataset's query or instruction (QMSum query, CNN/DM highlights instruction, docstring description), "Keep what is needed to answer this question: …" for QA, "Keep what is needed for this request: …" for extraction, and "Keep the whole … so that it can be reproduced exactly" for reconstruction |
| `writer.instructions_general` | the purpose-free form, for purpose-sensitivity contrasts |
| `writer.result_type` | `Neuralese<string>`: `view`'s result is representation-generic over a string |
| `sources[].meta.artifact` | the artifact type, plus its format (csv, html, json, yaml, python function, bash output, …) |
| `sources[].exact_refs` | paths, identifiers and URLs a view must keep verbatim. A record's own extraction target is never listed, because a renderer shows exact refs beside the block and that would hand over the answer. Reconstruction records keep the full list, which makes identifier retention checkable on the reconstruction |
| `target.kind` | `text`; `choice` (QuALITY letter); `calls` (xLAM gold calls as a JSON list) |
| `outcome` | always `gold`; `checked` is `identity`, `reference-answer`, `reference-summary`, `reference-labels` (LogHub's human-labelled event templates; target origin `dataset-labels`) or `code-computed:<method>` |
| `lineage` | project `upstream`, store = dataset, `upstream`/`upstream_id`/`upstream_revision` pinned, `teacher: null`; `notes` holds `artifact`, `view_call` (`view(x)`, `view(x, instructions)`, `ask(view(x), question)`), `target_origin` and the extractor or question id |
| `license` | per record: SPDX (a `LicenseRef-…` when the dataset states none or a custom licence) plus notes on the underlying content; `lineage.notes.license_provenance` holds the facts (§6) |
| `split`, `split_groups` | see §4 |

Code-computed targets (`view_extract.py`, all deterministic):

| Artifact | Extractors |
| --- | --- |
| JSON/YAML | value at a JSONPath (`$.a.b[0]["key with space"]`); keys of an object, in order; length of an array; the path of a unique string value. YAML is addressed as its parsed data; files with non-JSON scalars (dates, sets) are rejected |
| HTML | a CSS selector subset (type, `.class`, `#id`, `[attr]`, `[attr="v"]`, descendant and `>`): `title` text; text of every `h1`/`h2`/`h3`/`th`/`li` (2–12 matches); every `a[href]`; the text of a unique `#id`; the number of `table tr` |
| Tables (CSV) | number of data rows; a cell looked up by a unique key column; the key with the largest value of a numeric column |
| Python | parameters in order; called names, once each, in order of first appearance (`ast`) |
| Tool output | exit code; failing test ids; pytest's summary counts; the last traceback's exception and innermost frame; grep-hit files and count |

## 3. Source-specific choices

- **QMSum excerpts.** Most meetings exceed the 32k-character cap, so specific queries use excerpts. Queries are packed
  in turn order into windows that fit, so several queries over one window become purposes over one source. Each
  window is then padded with neighbouring turns, alternately before and after, to about three times its relevant
  text (at least 6,000 characters), so an excerpt is never just the answer's span. General queries are used only
  when the whole transcript fits. Queries that do not fit are counted as rejections.
- **CodeSearchNet.** The summary target is the docstring's first paragraph, and the docstring is removed from the
  source (with `pass` if the body would be empty). Docstrings that are not prose (parameter lists, doctests) are
  rejected. Reconstruction uses the whole function, docstring included.
- **WebSRC.** Pages are segments with `tid` attributes added by the dataset. These and scripts/styles are removed. The
  question's answer is the dataset's span or yes/no.
- **Repository configs.** The licence is read from the repository's top-level licence file at HEAD by a fixed set of
  text patterns (`view_extract.detect_license`: GNU licences by title, then MPL, EPL, Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD-2/3, ISC,
  Unlicense, CC0, Zlib, BSL, WTFPL) and recorded; a repository with no recognised licence text is kept with
  `LicenseRef-repository-content` (v3; v1/v2 kept only five permissive licences). Lock files, minified JSON and
  `node_modules`, `vendor`, `dist` and `build` paths are skipped.
- **arXiv and PubMed (v3).** The abstract is removed from the source (arXiv: every copy of the dataset's abstract
  string in the S2ORC text; PMC: the `## Abstract` section, kept in the YAML-headed Markdown otherwise) and a record
  is rejected if its first 120 characters remain. PMC articles whose abstract section has a `### Simple Summary`
  get a second purpose (a plain-language summary), so they are `compare` records.
- **BookSum (v3).** One source per `chapter_path` (single chapters and the dataset's chapter ranges); the summaries
  of the different study-guide sources are one target (seeded first) plus up to three alternatives.
- **Multi-News (v3).** Articles split on `|||||`, `NEWLINE_CHAR` turned into paragraph breaks, empty and
  duplicate articles dropped; at least two articles whose total fits the cap.
- **LogHub (v3).** Each system's 2k lines are cut into consecutive windows of at most 6,000 characters. A line is
  named by its shortest unique prefix (at least 30 characters) within the window. Whole systems are held out:
  two systems to test and one to validation, in hash order (`_loghub_split`).
- **Mind2Web (v3).** `reduce_dom` keeps the target element's subtree (at most half the cap), its ancestors, and
  each ancestor's other children nearest-first while they fit; `backend_node_id` attributes are then removed, so
  the answer is the dataset's action repr, not an id.
- **Common Crawl (v3).** Only HTTP 200 `text/html` responses; pages with replacement characters in their first
  2,000 characters are rejected (encoding).
- **Tool outputs.** At most two outputs per trajectory, from every eighth trajectory, in seeded row-group order. The
  purpose context is the command (`sources[].meta.command`, and the title).

## 4. Splits, groups and leakage

- Upstream splits are kept: test and validation never move to train. Sources with only a train split in use (SQuAD,
  WebSRC, xLAM, repository configs, the WTQ training set) get a deterministic carve by split group: 5% test and
  5% validation (`carve`). Tool outputs follow the harness bench's repository split (`split_of(repo, 5)`).
- Groups: `wiki:<title>` (SQuAD and FeTaQA, the same namespace as the S1 bgkit QA records), `repo:<owner/name>`
  (CodeSearchNet and configs, as S1), `swe-rebench-repo:` and `swe-rebench-instance:` (as the harness bench),
  `cnn_dailymail:`, `quality-doc:`, `qmsum-meeting:`, `websrc-site:` (a whole website), `xlam-tools:` (the tool set),
  `wtq-table:`; v3: `booksum-book:`, `xsum:`, `govreport:`, `multi_news:` (the article set), `arxiv:`, `pmc:`,
  `loghub-system:`, `mind2web-site:` and `mind2web-task:`, `cc-host:`. BookSum, XSum, GovReport and Multi-News keep
  their upstream splits; arXiv, PMC, Mind2Web (train only) and Common Crawl are carved by group.
- Closure: union-find over groups (`splits.close`) together with the protected bgkit benchmark index
  (`bgkit-benchmarks.protected.json`, by normalised question hash and id). A protected hit pulls its whole component
  into test.
- Leakage: the writer's inputs never contain the target (`records.leakage`). Docstrings are removed from code
  sources, and extraction targets are never exact refs.
- Exact duplicates (same family, source, request and target) keep the first copy.

### 4.1 Cross-corpus closure and dedup (v2)

Published corpora are immutable, so a new corpus adapts to them (`scripts/neuralese_data/cross_corpus.py`):

1. **Which corpora.** Every registered corpus that shares sources with this one (registry scan of 2026-10-10):
   `s1-full-final-20261003` (bgkit SQuAD/QuALITY QA, `repo:` file and tool-digest records, xLAM, Spider/BIRD,
   SWE-rebench/Open-SWE/Nemotron/AgentTrove trajectories) and `harness-bench-swe-rebench-openhands-pi-records-20261010-v3`
   (the same SWE-rebench tool outputs). Derived corpora inherit their parent's splits (`s3-subset-20261005` from S1;
   the harness-bench text twins from v3) and need no index of their own.
2. **Index** (once per published corpus; `python -m neuralese_data.cross_corpus --corpus-id … --files … --out …`, under
   the ledger): one streaming pass, parallel over 256 MB byte ranges, records each group key's split, the
   finalizer's digest (`finalize._digest`) of every source text, of every question (consumer request + target) and
   of every whole example, and the finalizer's bottom-64 MinHash sketch (word 5-shingles) of every source text of a
   consume/reconstruct/compare record up to 60k characters. A source text seen under three or more groups is
   background (as in the finalizer) and never used as document identity. Indexes live on NVMe at
   `/home/werg/data/natlang-corpora/cross-corpus-index/<corpus-id>/` (`index.json` has the counts) and are published
   as registry snapshots `cross-corpus-index-<corpus-id>-v1` (kind `cross-corpus-index`, not training data; sync them
   with `scripts/sync_training_corpora.py`; `--cross-index` takes the id, `neuralese_data/cross_corpus_registry.py`). S1: 1,870,591
   records, 985,434 groups (no group in two splits), 5.45M source texts (16,265 background), 1.54M questions, 4.73M
   sketches; 23 minutes. Harness bench v3: 3,843 records, 769 groups.
3. **Apply** (in `build`, after validation): our records are closed internally by group keys plus links computed
   once per distinct source text (same source, same question when the request identifies it, near-duplicate source
   at estimated Jaccard ≥ 0.8; exact example duplicates dropped). Templated requests (code-computed extraction,
   reconstruction) never link by question, since equal answers over unrelated sources ("exit code 1") would chain
   them. Each component then collects the published splits it touches: a shared group key, an identical non-background
   source, an identical identifying question, or a near-duplicate published source. A component touching one
   published split takes it if its own upstream split (or a protected-benchmark hit, which means test) does not rank
   higher; otherwise, and when it touches two published splits, the whole component is dropped (the published side
   cannot move, and test never moves to train). A record whose whole example is already published is dropped.
4. **Check**: the build fails unless no kept record shares a group, non-background source or identifying question
   with a published record of another split (`cross_corpus.check`); the manifest's `closure` has every count.
5. **Group conventions for closure.** Groups follow S1 where the sources overlap: `wiki:`, `repo:`, `quality-doc:`,
   `sql-db:<dataset>:<db>`, `tool-schema:<sorted tool names>` (xLAM and ToolACE gained it in v2), and the SWE-rebench
   tool outputs carry both the harness bench's `swe-rebench-repo:`/`swe-rebench-instance:` and S1's
   `repo:`/`swe-instance:` keys.

Dry run on the v1 slice (25,067 records): 1,026 records left. 953 were exact examples already in S1 (816 SQuAD,
137 QuALITY: S1's bgkit QA asks the same questions over the same passages); 73 components could not be placed (32
CodeSearchNet and 32 repository-config records whose upstream test/validation repository S1 has in train, 8 config
records whose repository chains to two S1 splits). 407 records moved (SQuAD and configs to test, where S1 has them;
WebSRC/xLAM/CNN to validation). Links: 2,169 S1 groups, 2,070 harness groups, 1,378 same-source, 1,464 near-duplicate
sources, 953 same-question. No violations after closure. v1 itself is unchanged (immutable) and superseded by v2.

## 5. The first slice

Corpus `view-ask-slice-20261010-v1` (registry `training/neuralese_corpora.json`; immutable manifest

## 6. Licence provenance and open items

Owner rule 2026-10-10 (AGENTS.md): every dataset and model licence is acceptable, including copyleft,
non-commercial, unstated and scraped content. Licences are recorded as facts; nothing is omitted or held for its
licence. Every record carries `lineage.notes.license_provenance`: the dataset licence and where it was read, the
underlying content's licence and holder when known, a class (the most restrictive known licence: permissive,
attribution, share-alike, weak-copyleft, copyleft, noncommercial; `unverified` when the content's licence is not
stated) and short facts. The manifest's `license_provenance` counts records by class and by dataset.

## 7. Scaling up

Caps are per source (`view_corpus.DEFAULT_CAPS`, overridable with `--caps '{"codesearchnet": 20000}'`), together with
`--max-source-chars`, `QUESTIONS_PER_SOURCE` and `EXTRACTS_PER_SOURCE`. A larger build needs a new corpus id and
manifest; it never replaces a published one.

1. Done in v2: larger caps for the local sources; Spider/BIRD, S1 tool outputs, CodeSearchNet's other languages,
   TabFact and ToolACE added; cross-corpus closure and dedup (§4.1).
2. Done in v3: BookSum, XSum, GovReport, Multi-News (multi-source records), arXiv and PubMed Central from their
   original-text copies, LogHub, Mind2Web (DOM reduction), Common Crawl; repository configs under any licence.
3. Next: SWE-smith trajectories (register first), extraction for the non-Python CodeSearchNet languages, more of
   the local arXiv/PMC/Mind2Web files (v3 reads 2 of 179, 2 of 49 and 5 of 11), and a per-family leakage audit
   sample before admission. SQuAD and QuALITY add little beyond S1 (their QA is already there) and are not
   worth raising.
